The wind whipped through the narrow alley, tugging at the edges of her coat as Clara pressed against the damp brick wall. The scent of rain lingered in the air, mingling with the acrid tang of the nearby street vendor’s frying oil. She shivered, not just from the chill, but from the gnawing anxiety that had settled deep in her stomach. The soft patter of raindrops began to fall, a gentle percussion that only heightened her sense of urgency.

“Clara!” The sharp call of her name sliced through the murmur of the evening crowd. She turned, heart racing, to see Tom weaving through the throng, his face flushed with exertion. “You can’t just disappear like that!”

“I needed air,” she replied, her voice barely rising above the distant honking of car horns. Her eyes darted to the ground, avoiding his gaze. She could feel the heat of embarrassment creeping up her neck. “It was… too much.”

Tom stepped closer, his brow furrowed, the flickering neon lights from the nearby bar casting an uneasy glow across his features. “You’re going to have to talk to me eventually. We can’t keep pretending everything’s fine.” The earnestness in his voice made her heart twist, and she bit her lip, fighting the swell of emotions threatening to break free.

“I know,” she murmured, wrapping her arms around herself, feeling the cool fabric of her coat against her skin, a flimsy barrier against the world’s weight. “But right now, I just… I can’t.”

“Clara,” he said softly, reaching out as if to bridge the distance between them. His hand hovered in the space before her, unsure. “I’m here. You don’t have to carry this alone.”

She swallowed hard, the lump in her throat tightening. Rain began to fall in earnest now, drumming against the pavement
